launch_materiality.notes: Same-day launch; free macOS tier is publicly available, but AIVP cannot run it on the current Linux host.

criteria.name: Product specificity
criteria.notes: Official page accepts a photo and documents local LTX 2.5 generation plus avatar/reference kits; exact-ASIN fidelity and first-10-second distinctiveness are untested.

criteria.name: Output quality
criteria.notes: No AIVP hands-on output or independent benchmark artifact.

criteria.name: Control & consistency
criteria.notes: Tool surface and repeat-generation claims are documented, but three-run consistency is untested.

criteria.name: Workflow strength
criteria.notes: Official product documentation describes ingest, local indexing, search, agent-directed editing, graphics, reframing and final rendering through one MCP-first workflow.

criteria.name: Speed & reliability
criteria.notes: Vendor benchmark is not accepted as AIVP hands-on evidence; setup, render time and failure rate remain unknown.

criteria.name: Cost efficiency
criteria.notes: Free tier and no per-generation credits are documented, but free renders carry a COEY mark and AI video requires high-end Apple hardware; cost per usable output is unmeasured.

criteria.name: Commercial rights
criteria.notes: Master terms permit lawful commercial output use, subject to third-party component terms; LTX eligibility and input/likeness obligations must be checked per run.

criteria.name: Automation & integration
criteria.notes: GroundSlate is explicitly MCP-first and documents local tools plus export/render paths.

criteria.name: AU creator/SMB fit
criteria.notes: Online free access and USD pricing are documented; macOS 26/Apple-silicon requirements sharply narrow fit and AU-specific availability was not separately stated.

criteria.name: Monetization fit
criteria.notes: High-intent new-tool coverage is plausible; no affiliate programme was found or verified.

analysis: GroundSlate is a differentiated local, MCP-first editor and generation backend, but its strongest claims remain docs-only. The exact-product gate, output quality, consistency, render reliability and real cost are unresolved. The current AIVP Linux environment cannot execute the Mac-only pilot, and AI Video requires an M3-or-newer Max/Ultra Mac with 64 GB unified memory.
confidence_notes: Confidence C: primary product, pricing, terms and privacy documents plus vendor-issued launch release; zero AIVP hands-on runs.
